title: Meniscal Injury
case: Case: A 52-year-old woman has 3 weeks of inner knee pain after a deep squat while gardening. It swelled a little the next day. She feels catching when she turns and she can fully straighten the knee. Joint-line tenderness is present on the inner side and McMurray reproduces pain and a click. Lachman is normal. No fever.

Working diagnosis: medial meniscal tear, probably degenerative. Plan: education, exercise therapy for strength and function, avoid deep squats and twisting at first, reassess in 2 weeks, orthopaedic review if true locking or no improvement.

differentials.name: ACL injury
differentials.key: Pop, rapid swelling, giving way, positive Lachman

qa: Why is an MRI tear not enough to decide on surgery? Tears are common in people without pain and many degenerative tears improve with exercise, so symptoms and function guide the decision [Ref - to verify].
How do you tell true locking from pain-limited movement? A true block is a mechanical stop with a firm sensation, while pain-limited movement improves with relaxation and is softer.
A 20-year-old has a locked knee after a twist. What next? Urgent orthopaedic referral, because a displaced tear may need early surgery to protect the joint.
Why avoid deep squats initially? They load and compress the menisci and may provoke symptoms in a tear.
Why also test the ACL? ACL injuries often come with meniscal tears and change the treatment plan.

fields.Position: Supine with the knee bent to about 90 degrees and the foot supported
fields.Action: Find the joint line with the thumb, just above the tibial plateau, and press along the medial and lateral sides
fields.Positive: Localised tenderness that reproduces the familiar pain
fields.Supports: A positive result is one of the more useful findings for a meniscal source
fields.Limits: Also tender in osteoarthritis, MCL sprain and other conditions

fields.Purpose: Reproduce pain or a click as a torn meniscus is loaded by rotation
fields.Position: Supine, hip and knee fully flexed
fields.Action: Hold the heel and palpate the joint line. Rotate the shin outward and apply a varus stress to test the medial side; then rotate the shin inward and apply a valgus stress to test the lateral side. Extend the knee slowly while keeping the rotation
fields.Positive: Pain and a palpable click or clunk at the joint line
fields.Supports: Meniscal tear, particularly in the posterior part, when painful
fields.Limits: Moderate sensitivity, higher specificity in some reports; pain alone is less useful than a click with pain [Ref - to verify]
fields.Errors: Moving too fast; not holding the rotation; counting general pain as positive

fields.Purpose: Reproduce symptoms with a weight-bearing rotational load
fields.Position: Standing on the affected leg, holding the therapist's hands for balance; knee bent to about 20 degrees
fields.Action: The patient twists the body and knee inward and outward three times
fields.Positive: Pain or a sense of catching or locking at the joint line
fields.Supports: Meniscal tear when combined with joint-line tenderness
fields.Limits: Reported accuracy varies between studies [Ref - to verify]

redFlags.Finding: Locked knee: true block to full extension
redFlags.Why it matters: Displaced tear fragment blocking joint movement
redFlags.Urgency: Urgent to semi-urgent (early surgical opinion; the sooner the better)
redFlags.Immediate action: Do not force the knee; refer to orthopaedics

redFlags.Finding: Hot red swollen knee with fever
Gross instability, severe swelling, history of high-energy injury
redFlags.Immediate action: Check foot pulses and sensation; emergency services

redFlags.Finding: Inability to bear weight, bony tenderness, deformity

manual.name: Tibiofemoral mobilization
manual.finding: Stiffness without a true mechanical block
manual.stop: Pain increases or a mechanical block is found

manualNotes: Preferred starting choice: education and exercise. Manual therapy is a minor adjunct. Do not use manipulation or forced rotation techniques on a suspected meniscal tear. Do not claim that manual therapy can reposition a torn meniscus.

exercise.Exercise: Heel slides and gentle range work
exercise.Steps: Slide the heel toward the buttock, then straighten
exercise.Starting dose: 10 reps, a few times a day

exercise.Exercise: Quadriceps sets and straight leg raise
exercise.Steps: Tighten the thigh and lift the straight leg
Knee bend to about 60 degrees at first
Graded walk-to-run, then change of direction

exerciseNotes: Principle: for degenerative tears and many stable traumatic tears, exercise therapy is a first-line treatment [Ref - to verify]. Trials have shown that, for many people with a degenerative tear, exercise therapy gives results similar to arthroscopic partial meniscectomy and that surgery is not better for most [Ref - to verify]. Follow surgeon instructions after surgery.

Early avoidance: deep squats, kneeling and twisting on a planted foot until the knee tolerates daily activity without swelling or catching. No fixed date is set for returning to sport; use the criteria: no swelling, full range, good strength and control, and no mechanical symptoms [Ref - to verify].

After meniscal repair: protocols restrict weight-bearing, range and deep flexion for a period that depends on the repair type, so follow the surgeon. Return to sport is usually later than after partial meniscectomy [Ref - to verify].
After partial meniscectomy: rehabilitation is usually quicker, with progression guided by swelling and function.

modalities.name: Knee brace
modalities.indicated: Not routinely recommended; surgeon directed after repair

pathway: Any emergency or urgent flag? Yes: act as in Section G.
True mechanical block (locked knee)? Yes: urgent orthopaedic referral.
Twisting injury with joint-line pain and positive tests, no locking? Yes: working diagnosis is suspected traumatic meniscal tear. Screen for ACL and other injuries and discuss imaging with a doctor.
Older patient with gradual joint-line pain and osteoarthritis features? Yes: working diagnosis is degenerative meniscal tear in the context of knee OA. Start exercise-based care.
Persisting mechanical symptoms (true catching or locking) despite good rehabilitation? Yes: orthopaedic review.
Visit 1: screen flags and the extension block, check for ACL and MCL injury, explain the condition.
Early: control swelling, restore range, activate the quadriceps, walk normally.
Middle: progress strength and function with limited deep flexion under load at first.
